title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a new Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to coordinate and oversee investigations into cybersecurity and artificial‑intelligence incidents. It also includes other related provisions to support national security and technology policy.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, a government program designed to invest in AI research, development, and innovation. It also includes other provisions to support AI-related initiatives and address related policy matters.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution emphasizes that artificial intelligence systems must respect religious freedom and be guided by authoritative texts, ensuring that their decisions align with established beliefs and values. It also calls for full transparency in AI operations so that stakeholders can understand and trust how these systems work.

title: To require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: All entities that develop or deploy artificial intelligence must design and implement a human‑controlled shutdown mechanism in every AI system. This requirement ensures that if the system behaves unexpectedly or poses a danger, a human operator can immediately stop it to protect safety.

title: To require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: This policy requires every entity that develops or deploys artificial intelligence systems to embed a human‑controlled shutdown mechanism. The goal is to give operators the ability to instantly disable the AI if it behaves unexpectedly or poses a risk.

title: To establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy establishes a new Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI development, deployment, and policy coordination. It also lays out regulations for advanced AI systems to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability.

title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to organize prize competitions that encourage research into making AI systems easier to understand. The competitions also aim to improve defenses against malicious attacks on AI products and cover other related goals.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are employed to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The purpose is to provide lawmakers with transparency and oversight of AI‑driven intelligence activities within the framework of the law.

title: To authorize certain labor market data collection activities and to improve Federal measurement of the workforce impacts of artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy authorizes specific activities to collect labor‑market data and improves how the federal government measures the effects of AI on the workforce. It also covers other related matters to ensure a comprehensive approach to AI’s impact on jobs.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law that sets rules for creating and using AI systems that read, analyze, or interpret text data. It focuses on making these models transparent, ensuring they protect user privacy, and holding developers accountable for how the AI handles information.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy seeks to create a federal framework that puts people first when using artificial intelligence in schools and the workplace. It also aims to teach and learn AI responsibly, make AI‑ready training available to everyone, and protect the privacy of students and workers’ data.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from rising utility bills that result from the power usage of AI data centers. It proposes regulations and financial measures to limit or offset the energy cost impact on families.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a new government department that will lead research, development, and regulation of emerging technologies, especially AI, to keep the country competitive and innovative. It also sets out rules and oversight to ensure AI is safe, transparent, and used ethically, and provides funding and guidance for responsible technology deployment.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Department of Artificial Intelligence to centralize AI oversight and coordination. It also sets out rules and regulatory measures to manage advanced AI systems and addresses additional related policy matters.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill requires companies and organizations that develop or deploy artificial intelligence systems to disclose certain key information, such as the system’s purpose, training data, and potential impact. It also includes additional provisions that address other aspects of AI use, regulation, and compliance.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to ensure AI systems used by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs are developed and deployed responsibly, protecting veterans’ privacy and safety. It establishes standards for transparency, accountability, and ethical use of AI to improve veteran services while minimizing potential harms.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation aimed at curbing the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that pose significant risks to public safety and security. It seeks to establish regulatory safeguards, oversight mechanisms, and potential penalties to ensure AI technologies are aligned with ethical and legal standards.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to use artificial‑intelligence tools that are transparent, reliable, and fair when reviewing veterans’ benefit claims. It sets out rules for auditing the AI, handling errors, and giving claimants clear explanations of how AI decisions affect them.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a law that bans the use of certain artificial‑intelligence technologies in specific settings or industries. It restricts how these AI systems can be developed, deployed, or sold in order to protect public safety, privacy, and ethical standards.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes requirements for ensuring that artificial intelligence systems used by the defense sector are reliable, safe, and effective. It mandates regular reporting on AI performance, risks, and compliance with security standards to protect national security interests.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 aims to ensure that the Department of Veterans Affairs openly explains how AI systems are used and how they make decisions. It would require the VA to disclose the AI tools and processes it employs so veterans, regulators, and the public can understand, evaluate, and trust the technology.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also outlines related goals and responsibilities for implementing this AI‑driven cyber defense initiative.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law that aims to strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems by setting standards and best practices for developers and users. It requires companies to conduct regular security assessments, disclose vulnerabilities, and establish incident response protocols to protect critical infrastructure and national security.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act would prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to automatically deny Medicare claims. It aims to protect Medicare beneficiaries from having coverage decisions made solely by AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or operating new data centers used for AI training and deployment, in order to address concerns about their high energy use and environmental impact. It also outlines conditions for monitoring, compliance, and a future review of whether the moratorium should continue.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to curb unfair pricing practices by AI service providers, preventing them from overcharging consumers. It also aims to stop companies from using AI tools to manipulate wages, ensuring fair pay and protecting workers from algorithm-driven exploitation.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to prevent unauthorized copying, distribution, and use of AI models created in the United States by establishing legal penalties and protective measures. It likely outlines enforcement mechanisms, intellectual‑property safeguards, and cooperation between developers and regulators to protect AI technology.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for monitoring and studying how AI systems are used within judicial proceedings. It aims to ensure that AI applications in courts are transparent, accountable, and do not compromise fairness or due process.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 is a federal law that establishes guidelines and standards for small businesses on how to incorporate artificial intelligence into their operations. It seeks to balance encouraging innovation with safeguarding ethical use, protecting data privacy, and ensuring compliance with existing regulatory frameworks.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to prevent misleading use of artificial intelligence by requiring clear disclosure when AI is involved. It establishes rules and penalties to ensure that consumers are not tricked into thinking they are interacting with humans or that AI outputs are unbiased or accurate.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act seeks to create a single, nationwide set of rules for developing and using AI, so that all states follow the same safety and ethical standards. By doing this, the law aims to position the United States as a global leader in AI innovation while preventing a fragmented patchwork of local regulations.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes nationwide rules to help identify, evaluate, and reduce dangers linked to AI development and use. It promotes responsible AI innovation by demanding transparency, oversight, and strict risk‑management practices to protect public safety and privacy.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act seeks to make it easier for banks, insurers, and fintech companies to develop and test new AI tools by easing regulatory barriers and offering clear, flexible rules. It also sets standards to protect consumers, ensure data privacy, and prevent unfair or unsafe AI practices in the financial sector.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act is designed to strengthen AI research capabilities at Historically Black Colleges and Universities. It provides funding, resources, and partnerships to help HBCU faculty, students, and institutions lead in AI innovation and workforce development.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to embed AI education into school curricula so students understand how AI works and its societal impacts. It establishes guidelines for teachers, resources, and assessment methods to prepare learners for a future where AI is ubiquitous.
